subject: english-literature
title: Genres of the Stage
welcome_lead: Tragedy, comedy and history — Shakespeare worked in three grand genres. Walk their conventions.
meta_desc: Tragedy, comedy and history conventions in Shakespeare at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have surveyed the three Shakespearean genres — each with its own arc, register and audience contract.

concepts.def: Drama charting a noble protagonist's fall through hamartia toward death, often closing with restoration of order.
Drama of confused identities, often pastoral, ending in multiple marriages and social reconciliation.
Drama dramatising English monarchical politics (Richard II, Henry IV-V), blending tragedy and propaganda.
Plays such as The Tempest and The Winter's Tale combining tragic and comic elements with reconciliation.
Plays like Measure for Measure that resist neat tragic or comic categorisation.
Shakespeare frequently blends tragic and comic registers — the porter scene in Macbeth, gravediggers in Hamlet.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Shakespearean tragedy traces a noble protagonist's catastrophic descent. Hamartia (a tragic flaw) and external pressure converge.

The final scene often restores order — Fortinbras's arrival in Hamlet, Malcolm's coronation in Macbeth.

Comedies move through misrule (disguises, crossed lovers) into restoration. Most end with multiple weddings — the marriage plot enacts social healing.

The 'green world' (Northrop Frye) — forests and islands — is the comic stage of transformation.
The history plays dramatise dynastic struggle for Tudor audiences. They blur genres — Henry IV mixes tragic kingship with Falstaff's comic excess.
